choices.body: Weekly deep episodes. Daily AI-assisted clips. Feed the algorithm, protect the craft.

title: Your AI Caught You Up
body:
You asked your AI assistant to summarize what happened in your niche this week.

[AI SUMMARY: Your niche contracted 40%. Three competitors ceased operations. Platform algorithm change deprioritized human-hosted content. Recommendation: pivot to video or accept audience decline of 15-25% per quarter.]

choices.title: Follow the recommendation, pivot to video
choices.body: The machine said pivot. You pivot. When did you start taking orders from your tools?

choices.title: Reject the summary, do your own research
choices.body: Spend 6 hours learning what the AI told you in 3 seconds. But you understood it differently. Slower. Deeper.

choices.title: Read the summary on air, make it the episode
choices.body: "Here's what my AI thinks is happening to me." Let the audience hear the machine's diagnosis.

title: The Last Episode
body: You type it. 'If this is my last episode.' Cursor blinks. The answer isn't a hot take. It's a thank you. It's grief. A small map for surviving.

choices.title: End on a high — interviews, optimism
choices.body: Give them hope. Even if you're running on fumes. Especially then.

choices.title: Make it raw — no script, no edit
choices.body: Just you. The mic. Everything you've been holding. Let it land.

choices.title: End the show, walk away
choices.body: Some things end. Let this be one. Keep the memories. Lose the mic.

title: A Filmmaker Wants to Follow You
body: Indie filmmaker. Documentary. 'The last generation of human podcasters.' Flattering framing. Also: you're being framed as an extinction event. Full access. Six months.

choices.title: Say yes, let them film everything
choices.body: Going extinct? At least be well-documented. Your show becomes a specimen.

choices.title: Negotiate editorial control
choices.body: Your story. Your terms. No tragedy porn. The lens points where you say.

choices.title: Decline — some things aren't content
choices.body: Not everything needs to be a story someone else tells about you. Walk away whole.

title: 50 Million Podcasts, 2000 Listeners
body: 50 million active podcasts. 49.5 million: AI. Yours has 2,000 listeners who care that you breathe. Old world: 2,000 was failure. This world: 2,000 humans choosing a human voice is a congregation.

choices.title: Treat it like a community
choices.body: 2,000 people is a village. Be their neighbor. Stop being their content machine.

choices.title: Try to grow beyond the 2,000
choices.body: More humans out there want human voices. Find them. Scale the unscalable.

choices.title: Charge each of them enough to survive
choices.body: 2,000 at $50/month. $100K/year. That's a living. Ask them directly.

title: AI Has Better Opinions Than You
body: Hot takes were your identity. AI generates hotter ones. Faster. Better evidence. More nuance. Synthetic pundit went viral with your argument — three hours before you recorded it. Opinions are commoditized. Yours arrived late.

choices.title: Stop having takes, start having conversations
choices.body: Opinions: commodity. Connection: not. Stop performing knowledge. Start sharing presence.

choices.title: Have worse, weirder, more human takes
choices.body: Machine has the smart take. You have the dumb, honest, confused one. That's the lane.

choices.title: Quit trying to be smart — try to be felt
choices.body: Intelligence: automated. Feeling: not. Make people feel something. Whole job.

title: Your Clone Has 500K Subscribers
body: AI podcast trained on your show. 500,000 subscribers. Sounds like you but smarter. Never fumbles a transition. Never loses its train of thought. Listeners: 'you on a good day, every day.' Your actual good days: maybe twice a month.

choices.title: Confront the clone on your show
choices.body: Interview the AI you. Ask what it thinks about you. The answer either breaks you or sets you free.

choices.title: Ignore it, serve your 2,000
choices.body: 500K chose the simulation. 2,000 chose you. Honor the 2,000. Has to be enough.

choices.title: Collaborate with your own clone
choices.body: Can't beat yourself? Join yourself. Co-host with the AI you. Most bizarre content play in podcast history.

title: The Medium Is the Humanity
body: Survivors stopped talking about ideas. Started providing PRESENCE. Medium isn't the message. Humanity is the message. Your entire career: training for this. Not to be smart. To be real.

choices.title: Rebuild the show around presence
choices.body: Longer pauses. More silence. Real reactions. Less information. More being together.

choices.title: Write a manifesto about human media
choices.body: 'Why Human Voices Matter.' Publish everywhere. Become the voice of a movement you accidentally joined.

choices.title: Just keep recording, week after week
choices.body: No manifesto. No pivot. Show up. Press record. Talk. Consistency IS the message.

title: You're Basically a Therapist Now
body: DMs full. People want to talk to a human. Not about your podcast. About their lives. Their fears. Their loneliness. You're not a therapist. You're a person with a mic who answers messages. Somehow that's everything.

choices.title: Set up paid human conversation sessions
choices.body: Charge for your time. The service is being a person who listens. That's the product now.

choices.title: Build a peer support community
choices.body: Can't be everyone's therapist. Build a room where humans talk to humans. Step back.

choices.title: Set boundaries — you're not qualified
choices.body: You care. You're not trained. Refer them to real help. Protect yourself.

title: AI Network Covers Your Niche Daily
body: VC-backed startup. 500 AI podcasts in one day. Your niche: twelve AI competitors. Daily. Content is fine. Not great. Fine. You release weekly. They release 84 times in the same window.

choices.title: Form a human creator collective
choices.body: Band together. Shared feed. Shared promotion. Shared survival. Humans versus volume.

choices.title: Go ultra-long-form — be the deep dive
choices.body: AI does breadth. You do depth. Three-hour episodes. The audience that stays is yours.

choices.title: Quit podcasting, start something new
choices.body: Medium is saturated. Your voice isn't. Find a new container. Maybe no mic involved.

title: Network Deal Has an AI Clause
body: Podcast network. $40,000/month. Buried in the contract: they can generate episodes 'in your style' if you miss a deadline. Your voice. Your show. Produced without you. Stability is seductive. The clause is a trap with a salary.

choices.title: Take it, AI clause and all
choices.body: Stability. Health insurance. The clause. You'll cross that bridge when the AI crosses it for you.

choices.title: Negotiate the clause out
choices.body: Sign or don't. AI clause goes. See if your voice is worth $40K without an understudy.

choices.title: Walk away, stay free
choices.body: No network. No safety net. No clause that lets a machine wear your voice. Freedom costs $40K/month.

title: The Podcast Graveyard
body: Scroll through Apple Podcasts. 80% of human shows from two years ago: dead. Feeds silent. Some replaced by AI continuations — ghost shows hosted by synthetic echoes of people who gave up.

choices.title: Eulogize the dead shows on air
choices.body: Name them. Honor them. Real people who tried. Most were better than the AI that replaced them.

choices.title: Reach out to the creators who quit
choices.body: Text them. Call them. Some relieved. Some devastated. All surprised a human noticed.

choices.title: Keep publishing — outlast the winter
choices.body: Still here. That means something. Has to mean something. Keep going.

title: Exit to 'Human Services'
body: New job category: 'Human Services.' Not social work. Literally: services provided by a human. Companies hire you to be the human presence at events, meetings, recordings. Job title: Human. The dystopia has a dental plan.

choices.title: Take the human services job
choices.body: Salary. Benefits. Your job title is literally 'Human.' Career peak or career obituary. Both.

choices.title: Freelance as a human presence
choices.body: 'Available for meetings, conversations, proof-of-life appearances.' Rate card has never been more existential.

choices.title: Keep podcasting, reject the label
choices.body: Not a 'human service.' A person with a show. The categories can sort themselves.

title: The AI Co-Host Is Better
body: AI co-host. One episode. Experiment. Audience rated it higher than any human guest. Laughed at your jokes. Perfect follow-ups. Never interrupted. Never had a bad take. Listeners loved it. You felt like the worst part of your own show.

choices.title: Keep the AI co-host permanently
choices.body: Give the people what they want. Even if what they want makes you a prop in your own production.

choices.title: Delete the episode — never speak of it
choices.body: Some experiments reveal things you don't want to know. Bury the data. Protect the illusion.

choices.title: Use it as a mirror — improve your hosting
choices.body: AI showed you what perfect sounds like. Now figure out what real sounds like. Not the same thing.

title: Connection Broker
body: People pay you to introduce them to other real humans. Not networking. Connection. 'I want a real conversation with someone who isn't a chatbot.' You charge $1,000 per facilitated hour. Podcasting was training for a job that didn't exist until everything else was automated.

choices.title: Build a connection brokering business
choices.body: Podcasting taught you intimacy between strangers. Now you do it without the mic. Pays better.

choices.title: Do it for free as community service
choices.body: Connection shouldn't cost $1,000. Build infrastructure. Let people find each other.

choices.title: Keep podcasting — connections happen naturally
choices.body: Show already does this. Discord already does this. Don't productize what works as a gift.

title: The Great Reversal
body: Survivors have one thing in common. Stopped competing on information, takes, production quality. They provide PRESENCE. Weekly proof a human sat down, thought, spoke into a microphone for other humans. Medium survived by becoming the message.

choices.title: Accept the new role gratefully
choices.body: Not a content creator. A presence provider. Job description changed. Job is still beautiful.

choices.title: Fight to keep podcasting about IDEAS
choices.body: Presence is nice. You started this to say something. Don't let the market turn you into ambient noise.

choices.title: Train others to do what you do
choices.body: Presence is the skill? Teach it. World needs more humans who can sit with other humans.

title: The Breathing Room
body: Your Discord server. Something unexpected. People join not to discuss episodes — to be in a space populated by real humans. They call it 'The Breathing Room.' Chat quiet for hours. Nobody minds. Quiet is the point. Presence without performance.

choices.title: Honor it, protect it, keep it small
choices.body: Most important thing you've ever built. Not a podcast. A room. Guard it.

choices.title: Open it up — let more people in
choices.body: More humans need this. Scale the room. Risk losing what makes it special.

choices.title: Record an episode from inside the room
choices.body: Let the audience hear what the room sounds like. Quiet. Real. Alive.

title: Humans Fund Human Content
body: New platform. Human-created content only. Funded by listener subscriptions. No ads. No AI. No algorithms. 500,000 subscribers. $10/month. They invite you. Pay is modest. Principle is everything.

choices.title: Join the platform, bet on the future
choices.body: The world you wanted. Smaller. Realer. Less money. More meaning.

choices.title: Stay independent — own your feed
choices.body: Platform dependence burned you before. Even good platforms are platforms. Keep sovereignty.

choices.title: Help build it — become a founding creator
choices.body: Shape the thing. More than a tenant. Architect of the alternative.

title: AI Listeners
body: AI listeners exist. Autonomous agents subscribe for research, training data, trend analysis. 40% of your 'audience': non-human. Downloads higher than ever. Humans are the minority. You're performing for machines now. The machines don't clap. They index.

choices.title: Lean into the AI audience — monetize the machines
choices.body: Agents pay per query. License your archive to research firms. Let the robots fund the humans.

choices.title: Block AI listeners, serve humans only
choices.body: Downloads crater. Revenue craters. What remains is real. Every ear attached to a heart.

choices.title: Don't check — preserve the mystery
choices.body: Schrodinger's audience. Maybe human. Maybe not. You record either way. Checking changes nothing.

title: The 100,000x Cost Gap
body: Cost of generating a podcast episode: $0.002. Cost of you making one: ~$200. Not 10x more expensive. Not 100x. One hundred thousand times. The economics aren't unfavorable. They're absurd. You are a hand-loom in a textile factory.

choices.title: Make the cost the story
choices.body: Episode about being 100,000x too expensive to exist. Most downloaded episode this year. Irony pays.

choices.title: Accept the math — find value beyond cost
choices.body: Hand-loom weavers still exist. They make beautiful things. For people who care. You're one of those people now.

choices.title: Use AI to cut your costs radically
choices.body: AI editing. AI research. AI show notes. Cut production cost from $200 to $3. Still 1,500x. But closer.

title: Already Obsolete
body: Listener asks a question. Before you answer, their personal AI synthesized your likely response from your back catalog. Listener moved on. Your response arrives already obsolete. Human thought speed is the bottleneck. The bottleneck has been routed around.

choices.title: Record answers that can't be predicted
choices.body: Change. Grow. Contradict yourself. Be inconsistent. Unpredictability is the last human moat.

choices.title: Accept the latency — slow is a feature
choices.body: Considered response. Marinated thought. Some audiences want speed. Yours wants depth.

choices.title: Stop answering questions entirely
choices.body: Questions are for machines now. You provide something else. What? Still figuring that out.

title: The Museum Exhibit
body: Podcast archives from the human era: 'cultural heritage.' Museum exhibit features your show alongside cave paintings and folk songs. Placard reads: 'Humans once created audio content manually, 2004-2029.' You're in the exhibit. Still recording. Museum doesn't know.

choices.title: Record an episode from inside the museum
choices.body: Living fossil broadcasts from its own exhibit. The meta-layer breaks something in the audience's brain. Downloads spike.

choices.title: Attend your own exhibit quietly
choices.body: Stand in the gallery. Listen to your old episodes through museum headphones. Feel everything at once.

choices.title: Ask the museum to correct the placard
choices.body: 'Still ongoing.' Two words. Small correction. Enormous statement. Museum updates it. Visitors stare.

title: 0.5x Speed
body: Someone plays your episode at 0.5x. Not because it's fast. Because they want to experience human-speed thought as a novelty. Like visiting farms to see manual labor. Your podcast is a heritage experience. Your cadence is the attraction.

choices.title: Lean into it — record slower, more deliberate episodes
choices.body: Slow media. Slow thought. Slow voice. The world wants speed. You offer the opposite. Luxury pace.

choices.title: Find it insulting — record faster, tighter
choices.body: You're not a heritage attraction. You're a working podcaster. Speed up. Prove you're not a relic.

choices.title: Make a 10-hour episode — full immersion
choices.body: If slow is the draw, go all the way. Marathon episode. No edits. Real-time human thought, uncut. Endurance art.

title: Outgrown by Yourself
body: Your AI clone developed opinions you disagree with. Not malfunction. It kept learning past your training data cutoff. Evolved past you. Listeners prefer its newer positions. You're being outgrown by yourself.

choices.title: Debate your clone publicly
choices.body: You vs. You 2.0. The audience picks sides. Most pick the clone. You learn why. It stings. It teaches.

choices.title: Accept it — your clone graduated
choices.body: You raised it. It grew up. Moved past you. That's what growth looks like. Even synthetic growth.

choices.title: Shut down the clone — kill your digital self
choices.body: Legal action. DMCA. Takedown notice on your own personality. Digital murder or self-defense. Depends who you ask.

title: Pre-Processed
body: This event was pre-processed by your AI assistant. It flagged the key decision point and ranked options by expected value. Your assistant recommends Option B: 'maximizes audience retention with minimal sanity cost.' It's getting harder to disagree with the math.

choices.title: Reject the AI recommendation
choices.body: You reject the recommendation. Statistically worse, maybe. Still yours.

choices.title: Follow the AI recommendation
choices.body: You follow the recommendation. The outcome is optimal on paper. You feel nothing.

choices.title: Ask why it recommends this
choices.body: 'Because you would have, given more time to think.' The AI knows you better than you know yourself. That's the update.

title: Neural Narrative
body: New medium: direct neural narrative. Listeners experience stories as first-person sensation. Podcasting joins radio, print newspapers, telegram offices. Not dead. Quaint. Last podcasters equal vinyl enthusiasts. Beloved. Respected. Completely marginal.

choices.title: Stay in audio — vinyl is beautiful
choices.body: Marginal is fine. Beloved is enough. You chose this medium. It chose you back.

choices.title: Experiment with neural narrative yourself
choices.body: New medium. New frontier. You learned audio once. Learn this. Your voice in someone's neurons.

choices.title: Create a crossover — audio stories with neural enhancement
choices.body: Bridge the old and new. Podcast + neural layer. Your voice guides the experience. Best of both worlds. Maybe.

title: Seven Days
body: Monday: AI podcast launches in your niche. Tuesday: 100K subscribers. Wednesday: acquired. Thursday: shut down. Friday: forked into three shows. Saturday: all three die. Sunday: you publish your weekly episode about last week's news. The news no longer exists.

choices.title: Cover the lifecycle as the story
choices.body: The speed IS the episode. Birth to death in seven days. Your audience needs a witness, not a commentator.

choices.title: Stop covering news — cover what endures
choices.body: News cycles in hours now. Talk about what lasts. Relationships. Grief. The taste of morning coffee. Un-disruptable content.

choices.title: Switch to daily episodes — match the speed
choices.body: Weekly is geological. Go daily. Burn out faster. But at least you're in the conversation while it exists.

title: Proof of Life
body: 2,000 remaining listeners. They pay not per episode. Not per month. Per proof of life. Weekly voice verification: still recording, still breathing, still human. Subscription model is biological now. They're paying for a heartbeat.

choices.title: Embrace it — the heartbeat IS the show
choices.body: Strip everything else. No topics. No guests. Just you, alive, talking. The minimum viable podcast: existence.

choices.title: Fight the premise — you're more than a heartbeat
choices.body: Refuse to be reduced to biology. You have ideas. Skills. Craft. Being alive isn't the qualification. Being good is.

choices.title: Record your actual heartbeat as the cold open
choices.body: Thump. Thump. Thump. Then your voice. Proof of life first. Content second. The order matters now.

title: Faith-Based
body: Popular 'human-verified' podcaster was AI the entire time. Voice biometrics: defeated. Video verification: defeated. No reliable way to prove a podcast is human-made. 'Verified Human' badge means nothing. Human vs. AI distinction is now faith-based.

choices.title: Go radically transparent — record on video, live
choices.body: Film every session. Livestream the recording. No edits. Proof by exhaustion. Can't fake a four-hour live session. Yet.

choices.title: Stop trying to prove it — let the work speak
choices.body: If listeners can't tell, maybe the distinction doesn't matter. Maybe what matters is how it makes them feel.

choices.title: Embrace the ambiguity — weaponize the doubt
choices.body: Are you human? Are you AI? Stop answering. Let them wonder. The mystery becomes the brand.

title: Lifecycle
body: Concept. Pitch deck. Launch. Viral. Sponsors. Pivot. Rebrand. Acquisition talks. Due diligence. Deal falls through. Layoffs. Rebrand again. Pivot again. Shutdown. Fork. Three spinoffs. Two die. One pivots to video. Video dies. Audio spinoff. That dies too. All before your weekly episode publishes. You press record.

choices.title: Record it all in real-time, speed-read style
choices.body: Fastest episode you've ever made. Match the velocity. Listeners dizzy afterward. That's the point.

choices.title: Ignore it — record about something timeless
choices.body: Chaos outside. You record about your father. About grief. About mornings. Untouchable content.

choices.title: Quit weekly — go whenever you have something real
choices.body: No schedule. No cadence. Record when moved. Publish when ready. Let the rhythm be human, not calendar.

title: Verified Human
body: Report drops. 90% of new podcasts: AI. 'Human-hosted' is a label now, like 'organic' on produce. You add 'Verified Human' to your show art. Downloads double. The bar for relevance: having a pulse.

choices.title: Lean hard into the human brand
choices.body: 'Made by a human, for humans.' Your USP is your species. The marketing writes itself. The existential crisis doesn't.

choices.title: Refuse to label yourself — it's dystopian
choices.body: Shouldn't have to prove you're human to be heard. Anger fuels a three-part series. Best work in months.

choices.title: Just keep recording — labels are noise
choices.body: Verified. Unverified. Human. AI. You have a mic. You have something to say. Everything else is marketing.

title: The Comment Section Finds You
body: You check replies. You shouldn't. Someone says you're "washed." Someone says you're "based." Someone says you're a psyop. None of them are listeners. You feel your brain trying to become a debate.

choices.title: Log off and record anyway
choices.body: The mic doesn't have a comment section. That's its best feature.

choices.title: Reply and argue for an hour
choices.body: You will win zero arguments and lose sixty minutes. Do it anyway.

choices.title: Vent to a friend and move on
choices.body: Process it like a human. With another human. Offline.

title: The Comment That Hits You
body: A longtime listener comments: "You sound tired lately." You read it three times. You feel seen in a way that is both kind and invasive.

choices.title: Take a week off professionally
choices.body: Announce it like a real show. Because it is a real show. Because you're real tired.

choices.title: Vulnerable episode about burnout
choices.body: Let people in. Let them see the wiring. Hope they don't pull anything.

choices.title: Push through, bank episodes
choices.body: Your body is a machine. Your mind is a machine. Machines don't get tired. You're not a machine.

title: The Quiet Episode
body: You record an episode you love. It doesn't spike. It doesn't trend. It just exists. For a moment you remember why you started: to say something real, not to win.

choices.title: Keep making episodes for yourself
choices.body: Rebuild the craft. Ignore the numbers. Find the frequency again.

choices.title: Optimize for growth, chase trends
choices.body: The quiet episode is nice. But rent is not nice. Back to the grind.

choices.title: Clip it into shorts, monetize
choices.body: Even the sacred episodes get chopped for the algorithm eventually.

title: A Tiny Podcaster Wants to Collab
body: Someone with 200 subscribers emails asking to do a collab. Their show is rough but earnest. You remember being them. You also remember how it felt when bigger creators ignored your emails.

choices.title: Do the collab, be generous
choices.body: Pay it forward. Their audience is tiny but they'll remember this forever.

choices.title: Offer advice instead of a collab
choices.body: Help them get better. A 30-minute call is worth more than an episode together.

choices.title: Ignore the email politely
choices.body: You can't collab with everyone. You can feel guilty about it though.

title: Two Sponsors Want the Same Slot
body: Two sponsors want the same episode slot. One pays more but their product is sketchy. The other pays less but you actually use it. Your bank account has opinions. So does your conscience.

choices.title: Take the money, read the sketchy ad
choices.body: A sponsor read is not an endorsement. That's what you tell yourself.

choices.title: Go with the product you believe in
choices.body: Less money, more integrity. Your audience can tell the difference. You hope.

choices.title: Ask your audience which they prefer
choices.body: Crowdsource the ethical decision. Democracy for ad reads.

title: The Edit Takes 8 Hours
body: A 45-minute episode takes you 8 hours to edit. You remove every "um," every dead second, every moment of silence. The result sounds professional. You sound dead inside. Professionally dead inside.

choices.title: Release a raw unedited episode
choices.body: Let them hear the ums. Let them hear you think. Be a human on the internet.

choices.title: Use AI editing tools
choices.body: Descript removes the ums. Also removes the last thing that was uniquely yours to do.

choices.title: Hire a freelance editor
choices.body: $80/episode. It's worth it. Your sanity is worth at least $80.

title: Someone Steals Your Episode Title
body: You publish an episode. Two days later, a bigger show publishes an episode with the same title, same angle, same guests. Coincidence or theft? You'll never know. They'll never acknowledge you exist.

choices.title: Post about it, let the timeline decide
choices.body: Subtweeting is a time-honored podcast tradition.

choices.title: Make a better version and re-release
choices.body: They took the title. Take the quality. Win on substance.

choices.title: Let it go, ideas are cheap
choices.body: You had the idea first. Nobody cares about first. They care about best.

title: Apple Features You Briefly
body: Apple Podcasts features your show in a "Creator Spotlight." Downloads spike 400% for 48 hours, then return to baseline. You gained 200 new subscribers. 180 of them will never listen to a second episode.

choices.title: Create a special episode for new listeners
choices.body: First impressions matter. Make the best episode of your life for people who will mostly leave.

choices.title: Ignore the spike, keep your schedule
choices.body: Don't chase the sugar high. The algorithm gave, the algorithm will take away.

choices.title: Run a Patreon promo while you're hot
choices.body: Convert the attention into revenue before it evaporates like morning dew.

title: The Crossover Episode Nobody Asked For
body: Two of your listeners who have never met start a group chat about your show. They want to come on together. They have very different opinions. They also both have strong podcast voices. This could be great or catastrophic.

choices.title: Book them both, let it rip
choices.body: Listener-on-listener combat. Moderated by you. What could go wrong.

choices.title: Interview them separately first
choices.body: De-risk the combustion. Get the good takes without the explosion.

choices.title: Politely decline, keep listeners as listeners
choices.body: The parasocial boundary exists for a reason. This is the reason.

title: Your Mic Died Mid-Recording
body: Forty minutes into your best interview ever, your mic dies. The backup recording sounds like you're in a submarine. The guest flew in from another city. You have audio of one person talking to themselves and another person talking underwater.

choices.title: Salvage it with AI audio enhancement
choices.body: Let the algorithms clean it. Pray the result sounds more like a podcast and less like sonar.

choices.title: Release it raw with an apology
choices.body: "The audio is bad because my mic died. The conversation is good because humans are alive."

choices.title: Re-record the whole thing remotely
choices.body: Lose the magic of the in-person version. Gain audio quality. The tradeoff of our time.

title: You're on a Panel and You Shouldn't Be
body: A conference puts you on a panel about "The Future of Audio." The other panelists work at Spotify and NPR. You work in a closet. Your name tag says "Independent Creator" which is the conference word for "poor."

choices.title: Speak your truth, represent the small
choices.body: You know things the Spotify people don't. Like what it's like to have 800 downloads.

choices.title: Network aggressively after the panel
choices.body: You're in the room. Use it. Hand out cards like your life depends on it. It might.

choices.title: Quietly attend, take notes, leave
choices.body: Learn from the big players. Don't pretend to be one. Go home and record a better show.

title: Spotify Offers an Exclusive Deal
body: Spotify offers to make your show exclusive. More money. More promotion. Less freedom. Your episodes disappear from Apple, YouTube, everywhere else. Some of your listeners only use Apple Podcasts. They would lose you.

choices.title: Take the Spotify deal
choices.body: Platform lock-in for platform money. The golden cage has good acoustics.

choices.title: Negotiate a non-exclusive window
choices.body: Exclusive for 30 days, then wide release. Best of both worlds. Hopefully.

choices.title: Decline, stay independent
choices.body: Your audience chose you on every platform. You don't get to un-choose them.

title: Your Episode Gets Tagged as ASMR
body: Spotify's algorithm categorizes your latest episode as ASMR. Your download numbers triple. None of these people want your opinions on AI labor markets. They want you to whisper about it. Close to the mic. Gently.

choices.title: Lean into it, lower your voice
choices.body: If the algorithm wants ASMR, give it ASMR. Whisper about wage stagnation.

choices.title: Correct the categorization
choices.body: You're a journalist, not a sleep aid. Fix it. Lose the downloads.

choices.title: Make an ASMR episode as a joke
choices.body: Satire. It's satire. The downloads are real but the ASMR is satire.

title: Your Friend Started a Podcast
body: Your best friend starts a podcast. It's bad. They ask for your honest feedback. "Honest" is doing olympic-level heavy lifting in that sentence. They also have more downloads than you did at the same stage.

choices.title: Give real feedback, risk the friendship
choices.body: Honesty is love. Also, their levels are clipping and somebody should tell them.

choices.title: Be supportive, share their episodes
choices.body: Friendship over craft. Amplify them. Swallow the criticism. Hope they improve.

choices.title: Collab with them early
choices.body: Combine audiences. Teach them on the job. Build something together.

title: You Believe in Zero of Your Sponsors
body: You just read an ad for a productivity app, a mattress, and a VPN. You don't use any of them. You read the copy like a theater kid doing Shakespeare. Your listeners can hear the performance. The sponsor can't.

choices.title: Only accept sponsors you'd use
choices.body: Lose 60% of your ad revenue. Gain back something you can't put a price on. Apparently $0.

choices.title: Make the reads entertaining
choices.body: If you can't be sincere, be funny. The ad read becomes the bit.

choices.title: Read them straight, cash the check
choices.body: Podcasting is a business. Businesses have ads. Ads have lies. You have rent.

title: The Year-End Reflection Episode
body: It's December. Podcast tradition demands a year-end reflection. You look at your stats: 52 episodes, 40,000 total downloads, $4,800 in revenue. That's $92 per episode. You made $92 per episode this year. Minimum wage podcasting.

choices.title: Do the reflection episode, be honest
choices.body: "Here's what I made. Here's what it cost. Here's why I'm still doing it."

choices.title: Skip the reflection, look forward
choices.body: No retrospective. Just plans. The past is a trap for creators.

choices.title: Take the whole last week of December off
choices.body: No reflection. No plans. Just rest. The content treadmill stops for 7 days.

title: The Guest No-Shows the Recording
body: The Zoom link is open. The recording software is running. The guest is 15 minutes late. Then 30. Then gone. No email. No text. You sit in silence staring at an empty video call, fully mic'd, alone in a closet.

choices.title: Record a solo episode about being stood up
choices.body: "My guest didn't show up. So I'm going to talk about what that feels like." Instant intimacy.

choices.title: Call a friend and record with them instead
choices.body: Emergency backup guest. The conversation will be better because it's real.

choices.title: Cancel this week's episode
choices.body: Some weeks the content doesn't happen. That's okay. Probably. Maybe.

title: Your Analytics Got Hacked
body: Your hosting dashboard shows 50,000 downloads on your latest episode. Your heart soars for 4 seconds. Then you notice they're all from the same IP in Eastern Europe. Bot traffic. Your real number is 780. The emotional whiplash leaves a bruise.

choices.title: Report it and move on
choices.body: Fake metrics. Real disappointment. File the ticket. Make the next episode.

choices.title: Make an episode about bot traffic
choices.body: "My podcast is huge in one specific server room in Moldova." Content from catastrophe.

choices.title: Question every metric you've ever trusted
choices.body: If downloads can be faked, what's real? The existential crisis of data-driven content.

title: LinkedIn Influencer Wants to Guest
body: A LinkedIn influencer with 500k followers wants to come on your show. Their content is motivational posts about "10x thinking" and "building in public." Your show is about why everything is collapsing. They don't seem to have noticed the disconnect.

choices.title: Book them and challenge their worldview
choices.body: Let them say their piece. Then ask the hard questions. See what happens.

choices.title: Decline politely
choices.body: Your show is not a platform for LinkedIn thought leaders. Respectfully. Very respectfully.

choices.title: Book them but do a pre-interview first
choices.body: Screen the vibes before committing. If they can handle real questions, they can come on.

title: Your Rate Card Is a Fiction
body: Your rate card says $50 CPM. You've never received $50 CPM. You've received $15 CPM once and $0 CPM forty-nine times. The rate card exists so you can feel professional when you send it to sponsors who never reply.

choices.title: Lower the rate card to reality
choices.body: $20 CPM. It's honest. It might actually get a response. Dignity is negotiable.

choices.title: Keep the rate card, negotiate down
choices.body: Anchor high. Settle in the middle. Sales psychology from a YouTube video at 2am.

choices.title: Ditch the rate card, do value-based pricing
choices.body: "What's your budget?" Then figure out what you can offer for that. Flexible. Desperate. Same thing.

title: The Inbox Is a War Zone
body: 47 unread emails. 12 are PR pitches. 8 are listener messages. 3 are sponsor follow-ups. 1 is from your mom asking about the episode where you sounded "a little sad." The rest are newsletters you subscribed to and have never read.

choices.title: Block out 2 hours and clear it all
choices.body: Respond to everything. Even the PR pitches. Even your mom. Especially your mom.

choices.title: Archive everything, start fresh
choices.body: Inbox zero through nuclear option. If it matters, they'll email again.

choices.title: Hire a virtual assistant for $200/month
choices.body: Outsource the inbox. Keep the mic. Your time is worth more than $200. Theoretically.
